chunks: And from him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Malik, from Zurarah, all of them, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Al-Mut'ah, by God, is superior; with it the Quran was revealed and the Sunnah proceeded."
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic and Sunnah basis for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts the superiority of al-Mut'ah, grounding its validity in both Quranic revelation and established Prophetic Sunnah, a claim central to Shia jurisprudential debates. This narration serves as a primary textual proof (hujjah) for the permissibility of temporary marriage, distinguishing it from permanent marriage through its specific scriptural and historical lineage. The emphasis on 'superiority' (afdhal) highlights its unique status as a distinct legal institution rather than a mere variant of permanent union.
